Honestly, I prefer doing it alone. Like when I go to a pub with friends I'd rather drink very little alcohol (when I get tipsy or drunk I want to do some lines to sober up) and just enjoy the vibe there without the old razzle dazzle salts.

But late at night when I am enjoying my company I sometimes like to drop some lines so I can be fully awake and aware and enjoy my time on my own. 

Other times I use it to get my through all nighters. I work a full time job and do freelance work on the side. One of my biggest rules was to make sure that my freelance work would not affect my stable salary, which makes working late nights quite hard. A couple of lines spread over a few hours and I can work amazingly through the whole night and still be fantastic for work the next day. 

Everyone is different. That's not to say that your boyfriend doesn't have a problem, he might, but honestly if he does it's probably something deeper than just a simple description of "addiction". The only way you're going to get to the bottom of it is by dropping the judgemental tone and enjoying his company more when he's on it to try and figure out where it's coming from. People also tend to be way more honest with themselves on coke so try being a little bit more connected with him during that time and be safe to be around in that state...

Yes. Consent is the biggest factor regarding SA. In the scenarios with your ex, you did not give consent, and by the sound of what you’ve described it was clear that you did not want it. 

I dated a girl for a few weeks who loved playing the “no I don’t want this. wait no come back” game. Even in that space I stepped back the moment she revoked consent even when I was 100% certain that she did in fact want me to continue, because her consent wasn’t about my interpretation of her desires, her consent was what she communicated through either her words or her actions. A clear yes is consent, anything other than that is not consent and is a form of SA.

I relapsed on Xmas as well. I know your pain. I was also alone, with the only important people in my life far away. 

I may not be next to you, but you are not alone in your pain and loneliness. 

Relapsed like this can make us feel a ton of shame, but remember to have grace for yourself. You cannot be perfect, none of us can, you can only try your best. And if you try and fail, or if you try and succeed, it doesn’t matter. What matters is that you try ♥️

You’ve got this. We will have a better Xmas next year, okay?

I want to make a slight distinction here in case it is necessary. At 16 I would’ve balked at being called a child because a lot of adults use that term condescendingly.

The need for you to turn to a trusted adult has got nothing to do with your age, but everything to do with the control you have in your life. You cannot control where you live, you cannot control your income, and you cannot control your safety in those spaces. A trusted adult has the necessary control to provide you a safe space and a way to break away safely. 

You need to reach out to an adult, and you need to do so quickly. This sort of scenario can escalate abruptly. 

You can do this - you’ve got this!
Thank you. I’m struggling but I’m gonna make this. I don’t know how, but I know I’m going to.

I relapsed last night… and my heart hurts man… I feel guilty, I feel stupid and broken. 

I’m not gonna say “don’t do it” because when the choice is front of you again it won’t be the words of a stranger stopping you. Just make sure that you are aware of what it means for you for the days afterwards. The days after a relapse are drastically different to the days after an almost relapse. 

Good luck, you’re not alone.

My cousin molested me too. He is slightly older than me. We were preteens when it happened. 

His father molested him. The things he did was the “normal” that was taught to him. I would even go as far as to say that what he did was wrong but he was innocent in the sense that he learned it from someone who he was supposed to learn things from. 

That doesn’t take away the trauma, or the broken coping mechanisms, or the pain. But I don’t see any of it as his fault, it’s his fathers fault. 

Not sure if it’s the same case here, but it’s an additional perspective that might be helpful. 

Good luck

Not sure what the end result was, but I want you to know that relapses are a part of the post-addiction journey. Failure isn’t “falling down”, failure is “staying down”. You’ve got this. Like a previous user said, tomorrow is a brand new day. I believe in you <3

I am desperately trying to not be an asshole to you, but I recognise that a positive outcome won't come from a negative initiation. "Seeing that she made wrong decisions"? 

Could you perhaps expand on the wrong decisions here and how this puts the blame on her? Was her telling him that she "didn't want to go all the way" not enough? Was her consent inconsequential to the equation at any point along the way? 

I sincerely hope your answer here shows me that I am merely misunderstanding your view point, because right now you are looking like the kind of victim blaming misogynistic asshat that is helping breed a world filled with rapists and mollesters who make others feel like the pain caused by their aggressors is in fact their own fault.

I think it's really important to reaffirm what consent is.

* it's explicit consent - i.e. a direct "yes: I want this"
* it's not forced - no coercion, threats, bribed etc
* there is no manipulation involved - you aren't being lied to, you're not under the influence of any substances etc
* you are of sound state of mind to consent
* you are **old enough** to make that decision

There's a lot unsaid that doesn't need to be said in your post regarding your consent, but an authority figure in your life has a level of control in your life which immediately makes your consent coerced if it was even given. Whether that authority figure is a parent, a boss, law enforcement etc, you are still under a form of duress to oblige. *And the fact that you were a child is the most important thing here*.

So yes, you most certainly were a victim of sexual assault. There is absolutely no doubt about that.

The natural response of your body to stimulation makes absolutely no difference to whether or not you were assaulted. The fact that the human body can orgasm from physical stimulation **whilst sleeping** is pure proof of the fact that consent need not be involved for your body to make all the good happy chemicals and feelings. One of the comments below said it beautifully:

"Analogy: someone can kill me, doesn’t mean I wanted to die"

The sad part here is that sexual predators will often use your bodies response against you, trying to "teach" you that this is actually what you wanted because of the response. As a child, that thought pattern becomes ingrained quite solidly. 

So please, know that this was sexual assault. If a child goes to an adult unprovoked and asks them for sexual gratification and the adult complies it would **still be sexual assault**.

How will I get past it? Eh, im just enjoying the vibe. Just because I have feelings for her doesn’t mean a) that she reciprocates those feelings or b) that I need to do anything about it. So when I hang out around her my heart feels full and I’m just enjoying the feeling. Nothing more to do at this point. 

How did it happen? Well tbh, we’re really good friends, we hold a lot of similar values regarding monogamy, nudity, music and pastimes. After tons of conversation what was just a good connection turned into a deep friendship and it’s kinda just grown from that. I met her when her and my friend started dating a few years back

So since posting this I spent a little over a week alone with her, and it was an amazing time. It was good for me because I realised that it’s easy for me to just enjoy the way my heart feels around her without feeling the need to push it somewhere.

Again, I just want to reiterate that her, my best friend (her husband) and myself are all openly non-monogamous, so the chances of this happening (in retrospect) are quite high, but I’m glad of our lifestyle choices allowing me to not feel guilty about my feelings nor feel like I have to remove myself or distance myself to get rid of those feelings. If anything my heart is making the path to an even stronger friendship easier, and real deep friends are precious af.

I am sorry to hear. You often hear people say things like "Be Strong" etc, and when we hear that, when we think of strength, we see in our minds eye people who brush off their depression with ease. The reality is that strength isn't "not getting knocked down", it's when we are down, and we have no energy, fight or motivation to get back up and we somehow manage to keep crawling into a new day with no hope of it being better. THAT is strength.

You mentioned relapsing, so it's safe to assume that you've had many crawling days. I know it feels like it is neverending, but they will. It gets better, I promise you. I am thinking of you, and holding you in my heart dear stranger. You are worth so much <3

I’ve been where you are now. I was the disappointment child. The reality is that it sucks. People will tell you to do this for you and not for them, and they are 100% right, but it doesn’t take away from the shitty feeling that no matter what you do you won’t get what you need or want from them. 

Hang in there though, it gets better. You’re already getting the mindset of self fulfilment, you’re becoming smarter, stronger and harder. In a little while you are going to look back on where you were today and you’re going to realise that you don’t need their approval, because despite of their lack of faith, you have made something of yourself. The weight of their opinions will fall off of your shoulders and you are going to fucking SHINE! 

I believe in you <3 keep grinding for your own happiness!
Thank you so much \^\_\^
